objective: 持续优化 EmbodiedForge 三个实际小时，保留既有工作，完成测量、回归、持续验证及可审查证据。
changes: Large plain native float64 Reach/Hold fields concatenate directly into the final owned float32 output when finite values fit float32 and underflow diagnostics are ignored, avoiding a full float64 concatenation result and subsequent cast allocation. Range reductions add overhead; allocation savings do not imply a time gain.

Position arrays with fewer than 16384 elements, mixed types, nonnative byte order, ndarray subclasses and diagnostic-sensitive float values retain the original concatenate-then-cast promotion, dispatch and FP diagnostics. Relative target subtraction remains unchanged.

156 regression cases cover threshold boundaries, empty inputs, layouts, independent owned output, input bytes, dtype promotion, subclass dispatch, special floating-point bits and FP diagnostic sequences. A reproducible task/complete-step benchmark is included.
scope: Synthetic CPU Reach/Hold task observations and complete camera-free VectorEnv.step. No GPU, MuJoCo, RSS limit or training-throughput inference.

performance_claims.primary: Separately traced transient allocation reduction in large native-float64 direct task.observe cases.
performance_claims.latency: Raw signed timings retained as shared-host observations; complete-step signed results vary by environment and include regressions, and are not presented as a general speedup.
performance_claims.pipeline_memory: Complete-step savings are separately shown and much smaller than direct task feature assembly; no propagation of the direct percentages to overall memory.

performance_caveats: Three Python/NumPy environments; 44 scenarios each, 21 alternating pairs, one pinned CPU on a shared host. All signed small-batch controls and layout variants retained.

Construction, warmup, tracing and byte comparisons excluded from timing. Later measurements may overlap separately pinned differential cohorts. Three independent tracemalloc peak samples; prebuilt inputs and runtime caches are outside tracing.

figure.scope: Separate direct task.observe and full-step allocation peaks at 8192 environments; no RSS or throughput claim.

persistence_control.scope: Isolated ENOSPC resilience control; does not classify earlier events.

inherited_diagnostics.interpretation: The prior MotionClips fingerprint event and previous round exit-120 persistence interruption remain unclassified. Their original records are retained. This round changes separate task feature assembly and does not classify or erase those events. The new isolated ENOSPC control verifies mirrored evidence behavior, not their historical cause.

round_scope: Three actual wall-clock hours include analysis, implementation, measurements, final-source regression and sustained differential validation, diagnostics and export. Per-cohort starts/durations are separate; parallel durations are not added.
ram_evidence_scope: Final cohorts mirror progress and failure bytes to /dev/shm before root writes and report exceptions directly through tool stderr. Mirrors are copied to the evidence archive after actual reaping.
evidence_selection: Raw measurements, source/harness snapshots, logs, input/output capture control, inherited diagnostic records, initial text files and final review files/figure retained. Initial binary assets and earlier compressed archives excluded; all their original hashes remain recorded.

data.name: task-numpy124
observations: Observed exit 143 is consistent with SIGTERM; the initiating sender/cause is unknown.
No task-failure report existed in either root or RAM mirror. Root and RAM progress reported zero persistence events.
Other two cohorts were still running when inspected. Approximately 31 GiB root filesystem and 23 GiB tmpfs space were available.
Interrupted progress is retained as incomplete; a restart must finish independently.

process_interruption.interpretation: One NumPy 1.24 cohort exited with observed code 143 without an application failure report. This round did not request termination; sender/cause remain unknown. The incomplete prefix is preserved separately and is not counted as a passed final cohort. The other two cohorts continued; the replacement cohort reports its own start and duration.

preserved.classification: Candidate reads subclass .size before confirming plain ndarray type. Initial implementation succeeds; candidate raises. Initial measurements, CI and incomplete cohorts retained as this candidate only; not final-source proof.

resolved_candidate_regression.interpretation: The first candidate inspected an ndarray subclass size property before confirming plain ndarray type. A reproducer showed the baseline passed and candidate raised. All three then-running cohorts were deliberately stopped and reaped, and their source/tests/measurements/logs were preserved separately. Type inspection now precedes size inspection. Final-source 156-case regressions, complete suites, measurements and cohorts were rerun; superseded results are not final-source evidence.

preserved.classification: Returned bits match for successful inputs; warning multiplicity and strict FloatingPointError priority differ for adversarial IEEE values. Raw records are retained, not counted as final proof.

resolved_fp_diagnostics.interpretation: Adversarial IEEE patterns exposed repeated cast warnings and differing strict FloatingPointError priority in the second candidate. Finite-range reductions now gate fused casts, and nonignored underflow diagnostics use the original path. All three final NumPy environments show exact returned bytes, warning sequences and FP exceptions across 2520 fresh-seeded cases each, including reversed/broadcast/unaligned layouts and signaling NaN payloads. Both superseded phases retain separate raw evidence; final source is measured and tested again.

data.interpretation: Two diagnostic modes across Reach/Hold prove the guards matter: the preserved unguarded candidate differs from baseline, while final source matches exact warnings and exception messages. Original candidate source is loaded into a separate module; workspace runtime source is unchanged.

preserved.classification: FP-safe 1024-row fast path retained exact outputs/diagnostics, but range reductions made 1024-row direct cases materially slower. Final threshold raised to 8192 rows; all final proof must be rerun.

threshold_tuning.interpretation: Range checks made the earlier 1024-row fast path materially slower. Raising the threshold keeps that batch size on the original path. Original measurements are preserved, and final boundary tests, differential configurations, diagnostics and all 132 performance scenarios were rerun. Large-batch allocation savings still do not imply a general latency improvement.

pipeline_latency_followup.interpretation: A follow-up was required by large negative original complete-step samples. It reuses warmed environments and longer samples on CPU 5, preserving construction-free steady-state timings separately. It does not erase the CPU-0 measurements or establish a general speedup; shared-host conditions and different fixture lifetimes limit causal attribution.

large_environment_probe.name: environment-large-py312
large_environment_probe.scope: Additional 8192-row camera-free Reach/Hold full-step trajectories with 1/4/16 substeps, forced terminal flags, readonly actions and partial resets. This exercises the final optimized path continuously; the original camera cohorts remain on smaller batch sizes.

signal_diagnostic_followup.parent_tracing: The final NumPy 1.24 cohort runs as a child of strace restricted to SIGTERM events. Existing-process attachment was denied; no kernel permissions were changed. The final trace is preserved in ram-mirror after reaping.
signal_diagnostic_followup.historical_cause: The earlier exit 143 remains unclassified; later successful runs or absence of a new signal do not identify the earlier sender.
